newsitem.title: MEXICO: Jailed Guatemala rebels in Mexico seek freedom.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Guatemala rebels in Mexico seek freedom.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-11-28

text.p: Six Guatemalan guerrillas jailed in Mexico for arms smuggling demanded their freedom on Thursday as part of an accord leading to the end of Guatemala's 36-year civil war.

"The Mexican authorities (should) consider our demand, showing a similar character as they have in foreign policy and in the valiant role they have played in the peace negotiations," a statement released to newspapers said.

The six rebels of the National Guatemalan Revolutionary Unit (URNG) were seized by the Mexican military in 1992 near the Guatemalan border with a shipment of arms. They have been in jail since in Tuxtla Gutierrez, capital of the southern state of Chiapas, with sentences from seven to 17 years.

On Dec. 29, the URNG and Guatemala's government are due to sign a final peace accord, leading to the handing in of rebel weapons, the scaling back of the army, and an end to the longest-running guerrilla war in Latin America, during which some 140,000 have been killed or forcibly "disappeared".

The peace accords have been negotiated in Mexico, under United Nations auspices. Diplomatic sources in Mexico said talks were continuing this week to hammer out final details. They said both sides were committed to making peace.

On Dec. 4, a ceasefire agreement is due to be signed in Oslo. On Dec. 7, one on electoral reform will be signed in Stockholm, and on Dec. 12 both sides will sign an agreement in Madrid on how to insert the guerrilla forces into political life.
The all-embracing Dec. 29 peace accord will then be signed in Guatemala City, with leaders from many countries expected to attend.
